verdict.rationale: CockroachDB's own docs and README say it survives disk, machine, rack and datacenter failures with no manual intervention, and that survival goals set how many simultaneous failures a database can tolerate. That covers the high-availability and failover half of the story. The ability to add read replicas is not documented first-party; only a community comment mentions follower reads, as an enterprise feature. Missing for 10: first-party docs on adding read replicas or follower reads, detailed failover mechanics (replication factor, leaseholder failover, recovery times), hands-on corroboration of failover behavior.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can add read replicas and rely on documented high-availability and failover behavior

citations.quote: It **scales** horizontally; **survives** disk, machine, rack, and even datacenter failures with minimal latency disruption and no manual intervention
_Survival goal_ dictates how many simultaneous failure(s) a database can survive.
I stopped using them when they released Follower-Reads as an enterprise feature.
